hook.situation: A friend says they cannot come, cannot eat meat, or do not want something. Korean needs different negative forms depending on whether the issue is choice, ability, absence, or careful clarification.
objectives: Choose 안 for simple choice or ordinary negation.
Choose 못 when something blocks the action: schedule, ability, rule, or health.
Use 없다 for absence and -지 않아요 for careful or more formal negation.
hook.whyItMatters: English 'not' hides several different Korean meanings. 안 가요 can sound like you are choosing not to go, while 못 가요 says you cannot go because something blocks you. That difference matters when declining invitations or explaining food restrictions.

grammarNotes.title: 안 + verb/adjective — simple negation
grammarNotes.func: Put 안 directly in front of a verb or adjective to make it negative. This is the everyday spoken negation: "I don't / it isn't." It states a choice or a plain fact, with no sense of being blocked or unable.

formTable.add: 안 in front of the word
안 splits IN: noun + 안 + 해요

examples.note: 안 sits right before 마셔요; a stated habit, not an inability. Pronounced [an ma.syeo.yo], no tensing.

examples.en: I'm not going to school today.
examples.note: A simple choice or plan; 안 negates 가요 directly.
안 also negates adjectives (무섭다 = scary), describing a plain quality.
With 운동하다, 안 goes BETWEEN the noun and 해요: 운동 안 해요, not 안 운동해요.

keyPoint.label: 안 vs 못
keyPoint.body: 안 = don't or won't, by choice or as a plain fact (안 가요, I'm not going). 못 = can't, blocked by an outside obstacle (못 가요, I can't go). If you simply chose not to, use 안; if something stops you, use 못.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 안 is pronounced [an] and, unlike 못, it does NOT tense the next sound. 안 가요 stays [an ga.yo], 안 봐요 stays [an bwa.yo]. Before a verb starting with ㅁ/ㄴ the nasal flows smoothly: 안 마셔요 → [an ma.syeo.yo]. No double-consonant tensing anywhere.

drill.instruction: Make each sentence negative using 안. Watch the 하다 verbs, where 안 goes between the noun and 해요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English speakers treat 공부하다 as one block and put 안 in front of the whole thing. But noun + 하다 verbs split: the noun stays, then 안, then 해요. So it's 공부 안 해요, 운동 안 해요, 요리 안 해요.

grammarNotes.title: 못 + verb — cannot, because something blocks you
grammarNotes.func: Put 못 in front of a verb to say you CANNOT do it — not because you don't want to, but because something blocks or prevents you (no time, no skill, no permission, an obstacle). 못 is used with action verbs, not with descriptive adjectives.

formTable.add: 못 in front of the verb
못 splits IN: noun + 못 + 해요

examples.en: I can't go today because I'm too busy.
examples.note: 못 = blocked by an outside reason (being busy), not a choice. Pronounced [몯 까요].
My body can't handle it — an inability, so 못, not 안.
하다 verb: 못 goes between 수영 and 해요. It's a lack of skill, hence 못.

examples.en: I couldn't sleep because it was noisy.
examples.note: An external obstacle (noise) prevented the action — a classic 못 situation, here in the past.

keyPoint.label: 못 + verb only (never adjectives)
keyPoint.body: 못 means 'unable to DO an action,' so it attaches to action verbs (못 가요, 못 먹어요). You can't be 'unable to be tall' or 'unable to be busy' — for adjectives use 안 (안 커요, 안 바빠요). 못 바빠요 is wrong.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 못 is written with final ㅅ but pronounced [몯]. Before a vowel it links: 못 와요 → [모 돠요]. Before ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ/ㅈ it TENSES the next sound: 못 가요 → [몯 까요], 못 봐요 → [몯 빠요]. That tensing is the audible signal of 못 — and the clearest way to tell it apart from 안.

drill.instruction: Rewrite using 못 to mean 'cannot.' For 하다 verbs, put 못 between the noun and 해요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 저는 안 수영해요 (when you mean you literally can't swim)
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'I don't swim' and 'I can't swim' look similar, so learners default to 안. But when an ability or obstacle is involved, Korean wants 못. 안 수영해요 means you choose not to; 수영 못 해요 means you're unable.

grammarNotes.title: -지 않아요 — the longer / written negation
grammarNotes.func: Attach -지 않아요 to a verb or adjective stem for the 'long form' of negation. It means the same as 안, but is a little more formal and is common in writing, careful speech, and longer sentences. It works smoothly with every verb and adjective, including 하다 verbs (no splitting).

examples.note: 먹다 → 먹지 않아요; same meaning as 안 먹어요 but sounds a touch more formal or written.
Works with adjectives too: 비싸다 → 비싸지 않아요 (= 안 비싸요).
A clean way to state a habit you don't do; common on forms and in polite explanations.
With 하다 verbs there is NO split: 운동하 + 지 않아요. Compare the spoken 운동 안 해요.

keyPoint.label: 안 vs -지 않아요
keyPoint.body: They mean the same thing. 안 먹어요 = 먹지 않아요 (I don't eat). 안 is short and spoken; -지 않아요 is longer and slightly more formal or written. Bonus: 하다 verbs DON'T split with -지 않아요 (운동하지 않아요), unlike 운동 안 해요.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 않아요 is pronounced [아나요] — the ㅎ in 않 is silent and the ㄴ links into the following vowel: 가지 않아요 → [가지 아나요]. The ㅎ never makes its own sound here.

drill.instruction: Convert each verb or adjective to the long negative with -지 않아요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Two errors are common: splitting 안 out as a separate word, and misspelling the ending. The fixed ending is one unit, -지 않아요 [지 아나요]. Don't insert 안 separately, and don't write 않어요.

grammarNotes.title: N이/가 없어요 — absence / "don't have"
grammarNotes.func: 없어요 is the verb for 'there isn't / I don't have.' It is the opposite of 있어요 (there is / have). The noun takes the subject marker 이/가, and 없어요 covers both 'don't possess' and 'isn't present / doesn't exist.'

examples.en: I don't have time right now.
examples.note: 시간 ends in a consonant, so 시간이; 없어요 = don't have. Pronounced [시가니 업써요].
차 ends in a vowel, so the marker is 가. 없어요 here means 'don't possess.'

examples.en: There's no milk in the fridge.
examples.note: Same 없어요 also means 'isn't there / doesn't exist' — the absence of a thing in a place. 우유 ends in a vowel → 우유가.

examples.en: I don't have any plans today.
examples.note: 없어요 negates having something (약속 = plans/an appointment); 약속 ends in a consonant → 약속이.

keyPoint.label: 없어요 vs 안 + verb
keyPoint.body: For NOT HAVING or NOT EXISTING, use 없어요, never 안 있어요. 안 있어요 is wrong. So 'no time' = 시간이 없어요 (○), not 시간이 안 있어요 (✗). 안 negates actions and qualities; 없어요 negates existence and possession.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 없어요 is pronounced [업써요]: the ㅂㅅ cluster keeps the ㅂ [p] sound, and the ㅅ links to the next vowel as a tense [ss]. So 시간이 없어요 → [시가니 업써요].

drill.instruction: Say you don't have each thing using 이/가 없어요. Choose the right marker by the noun's last sound.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English 'I don't have time' tempts learners to negate 있어요 with 안. Korean has a dedicated negative verb 없어요 for this; 안 있어요 sounds wrong to native ears. Memorize 있어요 ↔ 없어요 as a pair.

grammarNotes.title: Boundary check — 안 vs 못 vs 아니에요 vs 싫어요
grammarNotes.func: Korean splits the English word 'not' across several forms, and choosing the wrong one sounds off. This note sorts them: 안 = don't/won't (choice or fact), 못 = can't (blocked), 아니에요 = 'it's not [a noun]' (identity), 싫어요 = 'I don't like it / I don't want to' (dislike or refusal). Match the form to the meaning, not to the English word.

formTable.when: Choice / plain fact about an action or quality

examples.note: A choice or plan — plain negation of the action, so 안.

examples.en: I can't go today because I'm busy.
examples.note: Something blocks the action (being busy), so 못, not 안.
Saying a noun is NOT something uses 아니에요, never 안 — 안 가방이에요 is wrong.
Dislike, not inability: 싫어요. (못 먹어요 would mean 'I can't eat it.')

keyPoint.label: One English 'not,' four Korean choices
keyPoint.body: Ask what kind of 'not' it is. Action by choice → 안. Action blocked → 못. 'It's not [a noun]' → 아니에요. 'I don't like / don't want' → 싫어요. Picking by feeling, not by the English word, is the whole skill of this chapter.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 아니에요 → [아니에요], four clear syllables, no linking trick. 싫어요 → [시러요]: the ㅎ in 싫 is silent and the ㄹ links into the vowel, so it sounds like [시러요], not [실허요].

drill.instruction: Choose 안, 못, 아니에요, or 싫어요 for each meaning.
items: 'I'm not going today (I just won't)' → 오늘은 ____ 가요
'This isn't my phone' → 이건 제 폰이 ____

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 이건 제 가방 안 이에요 / 저는 그게 안 좋아요 (meaning 'I hate it')
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 이건 제 가방이 아니에요 / 저는 그게 싫어요
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Two traps: (1) you can't negate 이에요/예요 with 안 — to say a noun is NOT something, use 아니에요. (2) For strong dislike or refusal, 싫어요 is the natural word; 안 좋아요 just means 'not good,' which is milder and can sound evasive.

exampleSentence.ko: 안 가는 거예요, 아니면 못 가는 거예요?
exampleSentence.en: Are you choosing not to go, or are you unable to go?
I cannot eat meat because I have an allergy.
I do not exercise these days.
I cannot go because I do not have time.
I cannot go because of overtime.
I cannot eat it because I have an allergy.
It is not that I do not want to go.
I will reserve a different menu so it is not difficult.
I do not exercise these days.

extendedDialogue.setting: A friend clarifies whether a refusal is about choice, schedule, or a real restriction.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 오늘 모임에는 못 가요. 시간이 없어요.
lines.romanization: oneul moimeneun mot gayo. sigani eopseoyo.
lines.en: I cannot go to the gathering today. I do not have time.
lines.grammarNote: 못 marks the blocked action; 시간이 없어요 gives the absent resource.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 안 가는 거예요, 아니면 정말 못 가는 거예요?
lines.romanization: an ganeun geoyeyo, animyeon jeongmal mot ganeun geoyeyo?
lines.en: Are you choosing not to go, or are you really unable to go?
lines.grammarNote: This line directly contrasts 안 and 못.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 가기 싫은 건 아니에요. 야근 때문에 못 가요.
lines.romanization: gagi silheun geon anieyo. yageun ttaemune mot gayo.
lines.en: It is not that I do not want to go. I cannot go because of overtime.
lines.grammarNote: 아니에요 rejects the claim; 못 gives the real reason.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Then at the company dinner, do you not eat meat?
lines.grammarNote: 안 먹어요 asks about habit, choice, or preference.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 싫어서 안 먹는 게 아니라 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요.
lines.romanization: silheoseo an meongneun ge anira allereugiga isseoseo mot meogeoyo.
lines.en: It is not that I avoid it because I dislike it; I cannot eat it because I have an allergy.
lines.grammarNote: 알레르기 makes 못 the right choice.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 그럼 어렵지 않게 다른 메뉴로 예약할게요.
lines.romanization: geureom eoryeopji anke dareun menyuro yeyakhalgeyo.
lines.en: Then I will reserve a different menu so it is not difficult.
lines.grammarNote: -지 않게 gives a careful adjective negation.

readingText.title: 안 가요와 못 가요는 같은 말이 아니에요
readingText.body: 친구의 초대를 거절할 때 '안 가요'와 '못 가요'는 느낌이 달라요. '안 가요'는 내가 가지 않기로 한 선택처럼 들릴 수 있고, '못 가요'는 시간, 일, 건강 같은 이유 때문에 갈 수 없다는 뜻이에요. 그래서 '시간이 없어서 못 가요'라고 말하면 오해가 줄어요. 음식도 마찬가지예요. '고기는 안 먹어요'는 취향이나 습관처럼 들릴 수 있지만, '알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요'는 몸의 제한을 설명해요. 더 조심스럽게 말하고 싶을 때는 '싫지 않아요', '어렵지 않아요', '먹지 않아요'처럼 -지 않아요를 쓸 수 있어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: When declining an invitation, 안 가요 and 못 가요 do not feel the same. 안 가요 can sound like a choice, while 못 가요 says you cannot go because of time, work, health, or another limit. Food works similarly: 고기는 안 먹어요 may sound like preference or habit, but 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요 explains a physical restriction. For careful clarification, use -지 않아요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 안 가요는 어떤 느낌으로 들릴 수 있어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 내가 가지 않기로 한 선택처럼 들릴 수 있어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 알레르기가 있을 때 왜 못 먹어요가 자연스러워요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 취향이 아니라 몸의 제한 때문에 먹을 수 없다는 뜻이기 때문이에요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 조심스럽게 부정하거나 설명할 때 어떤 형태를 쓸 수 있어요?

culturalNote.title: Soft refusals often hide the exact negative
culturalNote.body: Korean speakers often soften refusals with phrases like 오늘은 좀 어려울 것 같아요 instead of a blunt 안 가요 or 못 가요. That phrase may mean 'I cannot make it' without naming the full reason. Still, when you do give a reason, choosing 안, 못, 없다, or -지 않다 correctly prevents misunderstanding.
culturalNote.tip: If the listener might think you simply do not want to, add the reason: 시간이 없어서 못 가요, 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence says circumstances make it impossible to go?
inlineExercises.explanation: 못 marks inability or a blocked situation.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence best explains a medical food restriction?
inlineExercises.explanation: 알레르기 is an outside restriction, so 못 먹어요 is natural.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses absence as the reason?
inlineExercises.explanation: 없어요 negates the existence/possession of time.

inlineExercises.prompt: Careful adjective negation: 이 일은 어렵____ 않아요.
Which pair correctly contrasts choice and inability?
inlineExercises.explanation: 안 often marks not doing or choosing not to; 못 marks inability or blocked action.

inlineExercises.prompt: 시간___ 없어요. (I do not have time.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 없어요 uses 이/가 for the thing that is absent. 시간 is not an object of an action here.
못 marks that something blocks the action. A meeting is the blocker, so 못 가요 is more natural than 안 가요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'I cannot eat meat because of an allergy.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 때문에 gives the medical reason, and 못 marks inability. 고기 is what cannot be eaten, so 고기를 is the object.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say carefully: 'This work is not difficult.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -지 않아요 is the longer, careful negative. It often sounds more measured than a short 안 negative.
The meat is the thing you cannot eat, so it takes 를. 가 would make meat the subject, which changes the structure.

bullets: 안: simple negative or choice, as in 오늘은 안 가요.
못: blocked action or inability, as in 시간이 없어서 못 가요.
-지 않아요: careful or written negation, as in 어렵지 않아요.
없어요: absence or not having, as in 시간이 없어요.
Do not translate every English 'not' the same way. Decide what is being denied.

writingTask.prompt: Write a short reply explaining why you can't join an outing today, using different negatives correctly.
writingTask.hint: Use 안 (don't/won't, a choice), 못 (can't, blocked), -지 않아요 (longer negation), and N이/가 없어요 (don't have): e.g. 시간이 없어요, 못 가요.
writingTask.model: 오늘은 시간이 없어요. 그래서 못 가요. 저는 고기를 안 먹어요. 운동도 별로 좋아하지 않아요.
writingTask.modelEn: I don't have time today. So I can't go. I don't eat meat. I don't really like exercise either.

canDo: Negate by choice or fact with 안 (안 먹어요)
Say you can't because something blocks you with 못 (시간이 없어서 못 가요)
Use the longer written negation -지 않아요 (좋아하지 않아요)
Express absence or 'don't have' with N이/가 없어요 (시간이 없어요)
